interactions.summary: A student cites an outside summary of Purgatory's sins as perverted, deficient, or excessive love, and Jiang agrees before restarting the reading and learning student names.
A student reads Canto 15, where reflected radiance overwhelms Dante's sight and an angelic messenger arrives to remove another wound and invite the next ascent.
Jiang asks why Virgil knows Purgatory's structure despite being pagan; a student answers with the poet's divine spark, and Jiang generalizes that poets and prophets share the same vocation.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang prompt, student answer, Jiang expansion, and a follow-up question.

speaker_notes.note: The student's trailing phrase after 'divine spark' is ASR-damaged, but the core claim about poetic prophetic access is clear from Jiang's acceptance.

claims.claim: The student summary Jiang affirms divides the sins of Purgatory into perverted love, deficient love, and excessive love, reinforcing love as the master key of the mountain.
In the Canto 15 passage, the angelic brightness functions as a purifying ascent marker by removing another P from Dante's forehead and making the climb easier.
claims.temporal_scope: Lecture interpretation of the reading on 2026-06-26.

claims.claim: Jiang accepts the student's claim that Virgil can know the path because the poet carries a divine spark.
Jiang makes the strong equivalence that all poets are prophets and all prophets are poets, extending the claim even to Jesus' speech in scripture as poetry.

signature_moments.moment: The angel's radiance is so intense that what first blinds Dante will soon become delight proportioned to his nature.
signature_moments.source_phrase: there will be no difficult for you but delight
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It turns purification into a training of perception rather than a merely punitive event.

signature_moments.moment: Poet and prophet are declared interchangeable vocations.
signature_moments.source_phrase: all poets are prophets all prophets are poets
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is a reusable Jiang thesis about revelation, literature, and authority.

signature_moments.moment: Virgil's pagan status is suspended by the fact that poetic sight still grants him navigational knowledge of the sacred world.
signature_moments.source_phrase: Virgil he is a pagan ... but he knows all how all this works
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It keeps the lecture's account of poetry tied to real epistemic access rather than decorative symbolism.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The poetic-prophetic capacity that lets Virgil perceive sacred structure despite his pagan status.
The beatitude chant heard during ascent, marking mercy as part of the purgatorial progression.
Jiang's shorthand for the incremental removal of the marks of sin as Dante ascends the mountain.

chronology_notes.note: This is the point in the June 26 class where the structural discussion of love yields back to close reading, and Jiang turns the reading into a larger claim about poetry as prophecy.
